P1.evidence: Three-part frame delivered cleanly — 'go into what you would like to achieve with your fitness where you're currently at. See if we can actually help you bridge that gap... If I feel like we can't really help you there. Also totally fine. I'll point you in the right direction.' Missing the fourth element. Agreement taken ('Okay. Fine. Fine.'). Open question run: 'what can we potentially actually help you with, SANKALP?'

P2.evidence: Injuries and current activity were covered thoroughly — but almost entirely because the prospect volunteered a four-minute clinical history unprompted, which under the scoring rule credits nothing. Age, height and weight were never asked. Diet, sleep and energy were never asked. Work status only surfaced through the money question. The prospect handed over psoriatic arthritis under active treatment and multi-level disc degeneration and the rep asked not one follow-up question about medication, clinician involvement or contraindication.

P3.evidence: Phase 3 was never run. There is no goals conversation anywhere in this transcript beyond restating the medical history back to him. No aesthetics or function question, no bridge to what is driving it, no impact on others, no reflection. The rep went from the injury summary straight to 'do you feel like you have finances set aside' at 00:07:31.

P4.evidence: Never run. Past attempts, what happened, why it did not stick and the root-cause question are all absent. The prospect's own account — that 24-48 hour shifts made a routine impossible — was accepted at face value and never explored.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. The only adjacent move was the timing challenge — 'Would you agree with me that life only will get busier when you actually have...' — which is Objection D material, not Phase 5, and which the prospect answered persuasively. No two-year picture, no settling question, no line in the sand, on a prospect actively accumulating new spinal pathology.

P6.evidence: Never run. No belief question, no all-in question. The rep asked instead 'what would you actually be able to put down today to start that coaching?' three separate times — a money question standing in for a commitment question, which is the inversion the phase order exists to prevent.

P11.evidence: No offer was presented and no close was attempted.

objection_plays.detail: 'Not the right time' was the substance of the prospect's position — start in 15-20 days, after a job. The rep ran exactly one OD move, the busy-season challenge: 'Would you agree with me that life only will get busier when you actually have...' The prospect rebutted it credibly (the job he is targeting has better hours than 24-48 hour shifts) and the rep dropped the play. None of the rest ran — no 'things never slow down', no compounding-cost frame, no 'what if all you had to do was show up'.

The money conversation ran, but backwards and at the wrong point in the call — at 00:07:31, before any goals, root cause, consequence or commitment work, and before any price had been named. Only the cash-on-hand element of the financial picture was taken. No isolation question, no 'you're not in a should-I place', no monthly surplus, no credit, no assets. The rep then used the answer to end the call. This is the sequence the coach criticised the next day.

The prospect's actual opening question was a clinical-fit question — 'I wanted to know how we could work through all these things... whether I can go forward with it or not.' There is no scripted play for it, which is the known script gap. The rep never answered it in either direction. He neither said the programme could accommodate the shoulder and spine, nor said it could not, nor suggested the prospect ask his treating clinician. He sent a workout video instead.

notes: Only Phase 1 and part of Phase 2 were run; Phases 3 through 6 do not appear at all. The rep pivoted to affordability at seven minutes and used the answer to close the call down. Two separate failures worth separating: the process failure the coach flagged the next day (qualifying on money before running the call) and the one nobody flagged — a physician described active psoriatic arthritis, an unrepaired rotator cuff tear and three levels of disc degeneration and was asked no clinical question and given a workout video.
